newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bonds, PIBOR start off GLOBEX lows.
newsitem.headline: French bonds, PIBOR start off GLOBEX lows.

text.p: French bond and interest rate futures kicked off pit-trading above earlier lows touched in an electronic trading session but while traders said there was no "panic" the mood was clearly nervous.
The catalyst for the selloff was the result of the first round of voting in a French parliamentary election in which the opposition left outpolled the ruling centre-right coalition.
Traders said although the strong showing by the left had caught many by surprise the fact the centre-right could still win a majority in the second round on June 1 was tempering the initial decline.
The June bond future bounced as high as 128.44 in pit-trading after touching 128.00 on GLOBEX, helped by buying from a U.S. house at the open, traders said.
Selling by a French brokerage on the highs then knocked the contract back to 128.28 at 0718 GMT, they said.
Technical analysts said 128.28 was a support level and below that 128.10/12 was another key area to be watched. They said a break below 128.00 would quickly bring 127.70 into range.
June PIBOR was also trading off GLOBEX lows, finding support at 96.20. It fell as low as 96.13 during an unusually busy GLOBEX session.
Some 18,000 lots were traded in the GLOBEX session between 0500 GMT and 0630 GMT, more than half the normal average daily volume for the entire day. At 0723 GMT some 41,000 lots had changed hands.
A trader at a money market broker said "the market wasn't position for last night's results".

French call money, a semi-official interest rate was unchanged at 3-1/8 1/4 percent, and the trader said he did not think the Bank of France had needed to exert any pressure to keep the overnight rate steady.

"The market has not yet done its full analysis of the situation. It has yet fully taken into account the importance of the three-way runoffs...there are lots of three-way runoffs and that increases the risks for the right," the money market broker said.
Three-month cash rates climbed to 3.49/61 percent from 3.35/45 percent late on Friday.
Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais, said the initial slump in PIBOR contracts would probably stabilise as long as the franc was held in check.
At 0731 GMT the franc was at 3.3752 against the mark, off an earlier low 3.3773.

French bonds underperformed their German counterparts across the yield curve. The 10-year spread narrowed to minus eight from minus 14 although it spiked as low as minus three during the initial slide.
The two-year spread widened 14 basis points to 28 while the five- and 30-year spreads both turned positive.
Analysts had said on Sunday night they expected the 10-year spread to move into single digits but were not convinced French yields would rise above the equivalent Bund yield.
